stem: When selecting an appropriate route for a medication, which factors should be considered?

options.A: The drug's pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic characteristics, route-specific indications or contraindications, and whether the client can safely use the route
options.B: Only the color of the medication container
options.D: The route should be chosen randomly because route does not influence drug delivery

rationale: Medication-route selection depends on drug characteristics, desired effect and route-specific advantages/limitations, as well as patient factors such as ability to swallow or tolerate the route.
educational_objective: Consider drug and patient factors when determining an appropriate medication route.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
source_locator: Route selection — indications/contraindications, pharmacokinetic considerations, and patient feasibility
source_claim_supported: Medication-route choice should account for drug properties, route indications/contraindications, and patient-specific feasibility.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration routes
correction_summary: Reclassified the item from Basic Care and Comfort to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies and eliminated oversimplified route-selection rules.
